Monica — I'm pulling the log slices now. Preliminary timeline from the serving plane (UTC):
- 03:35:12: first elevated token-error rate on primary pool
- 03:36:47: autoscaler triggered a redistribution of a subset of sessions to secondary pool
- 03:40:02 — 03:48:10: increased 5xx rate; some requests returned token-mismatch errors during cache warm-up
- 03:49:22: KV cache normalization completed; error rate returned to baseline by 03:50:05

I will export the detailed CSV (token-level timestamps, request ids) and attach it to the packet. ETA ~ 14:00 PST. Two notes: a) we saw a config rollout at 03:34:58 that was intended to tighten prefix caching TTL, and b) autoscaler piggybacked on the same control-plane window which increased session movement. Both likely contributed to the transient window.

I'll share the CSV named inference_timeline_20280822.csv as soon as it's ready.

— David
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Cobalt — need timeline + summary (internal)

Adding technical context for the customer packet: the rollout at 03:34:58 was a change to the prefix TTL for KV cache (TTL reduced from 600s to 120s) to improve memory churn for another customer class. The shorter TTL increased cache misses for long-running sessions on Cobalt's topology. When the autoscaler moved sessions to the secondary pool, those warm-starts collided with the low TTL and temporarily exposed token-population latency that surfaced as 5xx token errors.

Mitigations we are committing to:
- Revert the TTL change for Cobalt's dedicated routing policy (isolated immediately)
- Add a 60s staged rollout guard for cache-policy changes tied to active session counts
- Harden autoscaler to avoid concurrent session moves during control-plane rollouts (0.5–1 week engineering story)

I'll draft a short technical summary paragraph and include it in the RCA.

— Soojin
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@cobalt-pay.com>
Cc: ops@cobalt-pay.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Cobalt Payments — post-incident technical summary and timeline (draft)

Alex — thank you for your patience. Attached is a draft technical summary and the timeline CSV from our serving logs. Key points up front: 

- Incident window (UTC): 03:35:12–03:50:05 on 2028-08-22. Impact: transient 5xx rate increase affecting ~0.4% of your requests; observed effect on settlement batching for a subset of customers.
- Root cause (summary): a simultaneous configuration rollout (prefix TTL reduction) and autoscaler-driven session redistribution during the same control-plane window caused increased cache misses during warm-starts. This combination temporarily produced token-population latency that showed up as token-mismatch 5xx responses.
- Immediate actions taken: reverted TTL change for customer-scoped routing; rolled back the control-plane rollout for affected regions; increased trace retention for the window for audit.
- Committed mitigations: staged rollout guards for cache-policy changes (operational rule), autoscaler coordination guard (engineering ticket), and an extended verification run for Cobalt's routing policy. See action tracker below.

Attachments: cobalt_rca_v1.pdf (technical summary + audit notes), inference_timeline_20280822.csv (log-level timestamps and request ids).

Action tracker (summary):
1) Revert TTL for Cobalt routing — completed at 03:38 UTC (owner: Monica)
2) Add staged rollout guard — target: 2028-08-29 (owner: Soojin)
3) Autoscaler rollout safety (engineering story) — ETA: 2028-09-05 (owner: David)
4) Extended verification for Cobalt routing — scheduled window: 2028-08-25 02:00–04:00 UTC (owner: Monica)

Please confirm if you need any additional artifacts for your legal/compliance package. We can also schedule a 30-minute technical readout if helpful.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
